    Pyrifos: Mixed-Design Global-Null Maximum F

    pyrifos-mixed-maxF.Rmd

    The vegan::pyrifos experiment assigned one insecticide dose to each of 12 ditches and then sampled every ditch repeatedly. Dose comparisons therefore operate on ditch centroids, not on 132 independent observations. Phase 21 adds one shared whole-ditch permutation distribution for a family of such contrasts.

    ditch <- gl(12, 11, length = nrow(pyrifos))
dose_by_ditch <- c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.9, 0, 44, 6, 0.1, 44, 0.9, 0, 6)
dose <- factor(
  dose_by_ditch[ditch],
  levels = c(0, 0.1, 0.9, 6, 44),
  labels = c("control", "0.1", "0.9", "6", "44")
)
environment <- data.frame(ditch = ditch, dose = dose)
table(tapply(environment$dose, environment$ditch, unique))
#> 
#> 1 2 3 4 5 
#> 4 2 2 2 2

    All ditches have the same repeated-sample count, so complete ditches are exchangeable under the complete dose-null hypothesis. In an unequally sampled version, the same engine would restrict permutations to exact ditch-size strata and reject if those strata could not span every dose contrast.

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ dose + (1 | ditch),
  environment,
  vegdist(pyrifos, method = "bray")
)

    The planned family compares control with the average positive dose and lower with higher positive doses. Each observed statistic uses the ditch-centroid residual denominator. Every permitted whole-ditch rearrangement is shared across the family, and its largest pseudo-F forms the adjustment distribution.

    planned <- rbind(
  `control - positive-dose average` =
    c(control = -1, `0.1` = 0.25, `0.9` = 0.25, `6` = 0.25, `44` = 0.25),
  `low - high positive doses` =
    c(control = 0, `0.1` = 0.5, `0.9` = 0.5, `6` = -0.5, `44` = -0.5)
)

planned_fit <- permanova_mixed_maxT(
  design,
  contrasts = planned,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260722
)
planned_fit

    p_maxT controls familywise error only under the complete treatment-null randomization hypothesis: all dose-level ditch centroids are equal. That is a weak-FWER guarantee. Strong subset-null control is not claimed; Holm-adjusted permanova_mixed_contrasts() remains the explicit alternative when that strong-control contract is required.
